newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Italy seeks emergency UN session on Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy seeks emergency UN session on Albania.

text.p: Italy and Albania on Thursday asked for an emergency meeting of the U.N. Security Council, urging the 15-member body to issue a statement before possible massacres broke out in the Balkan state.

Albania's U.N. ambassador, Pellumb Kulla, said he wanted the council to "make an appeal to our population because the country is out of control and the people through this statement should have a source of optimism for the future."
He said the new Albanian government that included all political factions would welcome such a statement, adding: "It is very urgent to have this."
Italy's ambassador Paoli Fulci unsuccessfully urged members to issue an appeal before lunch so Albanians could hear it on their evening news programmes.

"Human life is more important than lunch," he said. "We think a real massacre could start any moment in Albania and we think it is important to assure the people that someone is working on the Albanian problem." All factions in Albania have asked for help, he said.

The Italian government on Thursday began to evacuate foreigners from Albania after arms depots in the capital Tirana and several other towns were looted and people used the weapons to raid food warehouses for emergency stockpiles.
More than 40 people have died in violence since January, initially sparked by the collapse of shady investment schemes which drew in the savings of hundreds of thousands.

Italy has already drawn up a draft statement for the council. It would request "all weapons and ammunition seized by citizens" be returned immediately. It would appeal to Albanians to refrain from the use of violence and reach a peaceful solution.

The Italian statement would also urge all U.N. members and international organisations to help search for a political solution to the Albanian crisis and it would call for an "urgent need to reopen all communication facilities in the country." Italy is not a council member this year.
Albanian authorities, buoyed by a new all-party government, have appealed unsuccessfully for calm against an unyielding campaign by rebels demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha.

Fighters in the south have said they would not give up their weapons until Berisha quit. In some parts of the south the rebellion visibly deteriorated into lawlessness with armed gangs roaming through rebel-held towns, robbing motorists, terrorising women and shooting at travelers.
